name: Have I Been Pwned – domain search
what: A service that shows which email addresses on a domain you control appear in known data breaches, after you prove you own the domain.
when: To find staff accounts exposed in third-party breaches so you can force password changes, check MFA and watch for phishing.
cost_note: Searching your own domain requires domain verification; larger domains normally need a paid subscription to see results.
example: Sign in to the HIBP dashboard and add your domain.
Verify ownership with one of the offered methods, such as a DNS record.
Review the breached addresses and which breach each one came from.
Make sure affected users have MFA and are not reusing the exposed password, and turn on notifications for new breaches.
pitfalls: Being in a breach does not mean your Microsoft 365 password leaked; it means the address did, maybe with a reused password.
Some sensitive breaches are only visible to verified owners.
Handle the result list as personal data.
